attractions.name: Khyber Pass
attractions.description: One of the most historically significant mountain passes in the world, used for millennia as the gateway between South and Central Asia, with dramatic views and old forts along the road.

attractions.name: Jamrud Fort
attractions.description: A 19th-century Sikh-era fort guarding the entrance to the Khyber Pass.

weather_info.climate_type: Mountain/alpine climate with cold winters and mild summers
weather_info.avoid_months: December to February (heavy snowfall, road closures)

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Mild and pleasant, 15-28°C, the main visiting season for mountain areas
Cold, often below freezing at higher elevations; heavy snowfall can close roads
Cool and scenic, good for travel with fewer crowds

travel_tips.tip: Visit Khyber in the warmer months (roughly May to September) if it's a mountain area, since roads can close in winter snow.
Shared vans (Suzuki/Hiace) and intercity coaches are the main way to reach and travel around the district.
Visiting the Khyber Pass area typically requires prior permission/coordination — check current local requirements before planning a trip.

history.founded: Historic since antiquity as the route of the Khyber Pass; formalized as Khyber Agency in 1878, merged as a regular KP district in 2018
history.city_history: Khyber District contains the legendary Khyber Pass, the historic gateway used by countless armies and traders — from Alexander the Great to the Mughals — connecting South Asia to Central Asia along the old Silk Road.
history.province_history: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (formerly North-West Frontier Province) has been a historic crossroads between South and Central Asia for millennia, home to Gandhara civilization sites, the ancient Silk Road route through the Khyber Pass, and a mix of Pashtun tribal, Mughal, Sikh, and British colonial influence before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947. In 2018, the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) were formally merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as regular districts.
